body:
Let's just use 0.1.3 (or 0.1.4)
Can you reproduce without --config=cuda?

I cannot and cannot seems to be able to configure cuda correctly on my machine.

`bazel build -c opt //tensorflow/tools/pip_package:build_pip_package` gives the same error.

(tested with bazel 0.1.3).
pulling in @dzc if he knows more about that. It's probably a git config issue

@zer0n: try adding --spawn_strategy=standalone

Also, I think as of this morning we now require bazel 0.1.4 because of internal changes made by the bazel team to start using labels for loading skylark extensions.

Thanks @vrv . Adding `--spawn_strategy=standalone` works.

FYI, bazel 0.1.4 also fails to build without the above option.
@damienmg: is there a bug we can point people as to why --spawn_strategy=standalone is required, and when it might be fixed?
FYI The jsch NoClassDefFoundError was a known issue for Bazel 0.1.1 (see #596) and was fixed in 916370ec6195d7fc13812e64a65c2cd6ef9e36c9 and should not be occurring anymore in the latest release.

@davidzchen Apparently, there was a regression in `bazel 0.1.3`. 

I got around that issue by commenting out this line in my `.gitconfig` file.

```
[url "ssh://git@github.com/"]
    insteadOf = https://github.com/
```
I found the problem. Commit 27760a6efefc64f9577ed1add120b60399203be3 inadvertently removed `//third_party/jsch` from the `runtime_deps`. I'll put together a patch for restoring that dependency.

The patch that restores the jsch `runtime_dep` should be out with the next push. Note that this will only fix the `NoClassDefFoundError`; the Git workspace rules currently only support cloning via HTTP but not via SSH. I have opened #810 for adding support for cloning via SSH.
The jsch NoClassDefFoundError is now fixed by cc9e445. The other issues seem to be separate problems.
